slides.title: Segmenting Consumer Markets
slides.text: Segmenting Consumer Markets
slides.notes:
Market segmentation divides a market into well-defined slices.
A market segment consists of a group of consumers who share a similar set of needs and/or profile characteristics.
Common types of segmentation include demographic, geographic, behavioral, and psychographic.
slides.visual_text: Heading Segmenting Consumer Markets with a cartoon crowd of many different people in varied clothing. Notes: market segmentation divides a market into well-defined slices; a market segment is a group of consumers who share a similar set of needs or profile characteristics; common types are demographic, geographic, behavioral and psychographic.

slides.text: Dividing a group of heterogenous customers with different needs into homogenous subgroups or segments with similar needs and preferences.

slides.title: Demographic Segmentation
slides.text:
Demographic Segmentation
Age
Life-cycle stage
Gender
Family size
Education
Income
Race and culture
slides.notes:
One reason demographic variables such as age, family size, family life cycle, gender, income, occupation, education, religion, race, generation, nationality, and social class are so popular with marketers is that they’re often associated with consumer needs and wants.
Another is that they’re easy to measure.

slides.title: Gender
slides.text:
Gender
Men and women have different attitudes and behave differently

bullets.text: Men and women have different attitudes and behave differently

slides.notes: Research shows that women have traditionally tended to be more communal-minded and men more self-expressive and goal-directed; women have tended to take in more of the data in their immediate environment and men to focus on the part of the environment that helps them achieve a goal. Gender differences are shrinking in some other areas as men and women expand their roles.

slides.title: Geographic Segmentation
slides.text:
Geographic Segmentation
Divides the market into geographic units such as nations, states, regions, countries, cities, or neighborhoods.

bullets.text: Divides the market into geographic units such as nations, states, regions, countries, cities, or neighborhoods.

slides.notes:
Geographic segmentation divides the market into geographic units such as nations, states, regions, counties, cities, or neighborhoods.
The company can operate in one or a few areas, or it can operate in all areas while heeding local variations. In that way, it can tailor marketing programs to the needs and wants of local customer groups in trading areas and neighborhoods, and it can even cater to the needs of individual customers.
Going online to reach customers in a particular geographic location can open a host of local opportunities, as Yelp has found out.
slides.visual_text: Geographic segmentation: divides the market into geographic units such as nations, states, regions, countries, cities or neighborhoods. A photo of a fast food meal (fries, burger, cup) with a golden arches logo.

slides.title: Behavioral Segmentation
slides.text:
Behavioral Segmentation
Marketers divide buyers into groups on the basis of their actions
User status- non users, potential users, first time users, regular users
Usage rate- light, medium, heavy
Buyer-readiness stage
Loyalty status- hard core, split loyal, shifting loyalty, switchers
Occasions

bullets.text: Marketers divide buyers into groups on the basis of their actions
User status- non users, potential users, first time users, regular users
Loyalty status- hard core, split loyal, shifting loyalty, switchers

slides.notes:
In behavioral segmentation, marketers divide buyers into groups on the basis of their actions.
Many marketers believe variables related to users or their usage—user status, usage rate, buyer-readiness stage, loyalty status, and occasions—are good starting points for constructing market segments.
slides.visual_text: Behavioral segmentation: marketers divide buyers into groups on the basis of their actions. User status (non users, potential users, first time users, regular users), usage rate (light, medium, heavy), buyer-readiness stage, loyalty status (hard core, split loyal, shifting loyalty, switchers), occasions. A picture of a Frequent flyer Rewards card with an aeroplane.

slides.title: Psychographic Segmentation
slides.text:
Psychographic Segmentation
Buyers are divided into groups on the basis of psychological traits, lifestyle, values, personality.
Intangible consumer characteristics such as Lifestyle, personality, interests, values.
Psychographic traits are not easily identifiable.

bullets.text: Buyers are divided into groups on the basis of psychological traits, lifestyle, values, personality.
Intangible consumer characteristics such as Lifestyle, personality, interests, values.
Psychographic traits are not easily identifiable.

slides.notes:
In psychographic segmentation, buyers are divided into groups on the basis of psychological traits, lifestyle, or values.
Psychographic segmentation is important because demographic, geographic, and behavioral characteristics of consumers do not always accurately reflect their underlying needs.
slides.visual_text: Psychographic segmentation: buyers divided on psychological traits, lifestyle, values, personality; intangible characteristics such as lifestyle, personality, interests, values; psychographic traits are not easily identifiable. Three pictures: an EATFIT Honestly Indian logo with a tiger wearing sunglasses, a Thums Up logo with the line Taste the Thunder, and a black cruiser motorcycle.

slides.title: Segmenting Business Markets
slides.text:
Segmenting Business Markets
Demographic factors- Industry, company size
Operating variables- Technology, Usage
Purchasing approaches- purchasing policies, dominant purchase criteria (Quality, service, price)
Situational factors- Urgency, Order size
Personal characteristics- Loyalty, Value similarity

bullets.text: Purchasing approaches- purchasing policies, dominant purchase criteria (Quality, service, price)

slides.notes: We can segment business markets with some of the same variables we use in consumer markets, such as geography, benefits sought, and usage rate, but business marketers also use other variables.

slides.title: Points of Difference and Points of Parity
slides.text:
Points of Difference and Points of Parity
Points of difference (P O D s)
Attributes/benefits that consumers strongly associate with a brand, positively evaluate, and believe they could not find to the same extent with a competitive brand.
Benefits that are unique to a company’s offering.
“Why should the consumer choose us instead of the alternatives?”

bullets.text: Points of difference (P O D s)
Attributes/benefits that consumers strongly associate with a brand, positively evaluate, and believe they could not find to the same extent with a competitive brand.
Benefits that are unique to a company’s offering.
“Why should the consumer choose us instead of the alternatives?”

slides.title: Points of Parity (P O P s)
slides.text:
Points of Parity (P O P s)
Attribute/benefit associations that are not necessarily unique to the brand but may in fact be shared with other brands
“What do we need to have in common with competitors to be considered a legitimate option?”
P O P forms
Category: Features necessary to belong to the category
Correlational: negative brand associations
Competitive: Features needed to neutralize a competitor's advantage

slides.title: Communicating the Positioning
slides.text:
Communicating the Positioning
Positioning statement
Communicating an offering’s category membership along with points of parity and points of difference, and developing a narrative to convey the offering’s positioning.
For health-conscious young professionals, Brand X is a convenient healthy meal solution that provides nutritious food without compromising taste because it uses fresh, locally sourced ingredients.
